name: The Clark household at 2000 Prairie Avenue
head: pa1904_clark_john_m

present_on_scene_date.note: Listed at 2000 Prairie Avenue in the Blue Book for 1904 (canvass begun September 1903) and again in the 1905 edition (canvass begun September 1904), which bracket 1 July 1904. The 1905 list prints: 2000 Mr. & Mrs. John M. Clark.

associated_with.note: The Blue Book's Prairie Avenue street list prints the household at 2000, and the 1905 list again. The book gives no date the household came or went, so neither end is dated here.

not_in_this_household.note: WHO IS NOT ON THIS CARD, AND WHY. The Blue Book is a society register: it names the family members who received and were received, prints unmarried daughters only as '& dr.', and names no young children, servants, coachmen, cooks or nurses. The 1900 census (ED 40, T623 roll 245) was read for this card. The four live-in staff it lists at the house on 1 June 1900 are on the card, graded inferred because the count was taken four years before the scene. The children the Blue Book lists at the number from 1890 to 1911 are on the card with the years each was listed, whether or not they were at home in 1904. The 1910 census was not read for this card. A person goes on this card when a source names them, and not before.

persons.name: John M. Clark
persons.note: The 1900 census lists John M. Clark here as head, born August 1837 (the figures are hard to read), in Canada (as read), married, president (company) (ED 40, sheet 9A, line 45, leaf n810).

born.note: Biographical date from the cited period publication(s). The earlier census transcription on this card is retained as a separate reading; where it disagrees, this figure uses the independently published biographical date. The publication date is not the date the photograph was taken.

portrait.caption: John M. Clark, undated photograph published in Men of Illinois (1902), p. 474.
portrait.why: Identified by the printed caption and checked against the household record. The monochrome photograph does not establish skin, eye or clothing colours.

persons.name: Mrs. John M. Clark
persons.note: The 1900 census lists Louise Clark here as wife, born January 1850, in New York, married (ED 40, sheet 9A, line 46, leaf n810).

born.note: The existing census transcription gives born January 1850. The year is carried into the age shown on this card.

portrait_research.note: An individual portrait has not yet been verified in the period portrait books and Glessner House Museum article archive searched for this project. Any figure shown is a reconstruction, not an attested likeness.

persons.name: Berthe Riches

born.note: The census gives May 1872, age 28 on 1 June 1900.

occupation.note: Written as "Ladies maid" in the occupation column on 1 June 1900.

persons.note: Enumerated on 1 June 1900 in the house, as a servant (ladies maid); born May 1872, in France, came to the United States in 1893, single. Servants changed places often, so this records who worked here in 1900; no source read says whether this person was still here on 1 July 1904. Part of the name is hard to read on the sheet; this is the best reading.
